title: Load a filled syringe into a syringe pump: flange in its slot, driver up to the plunger without pushing it
instruction: Load the filled syringe into the syringe pump. Lay it in the pump's cradle with the flange at the end of its barrel down in the flange slot, then slide the grey plunger driver along its track until it is up against the end of the plunger, without pushing the plunger in.
context: Nurses set up syringe pumps this way. The Medfusion 3500 quick reference guide, "Load syringe": "Make sure the flange on the syringe barrel is secure in the syringe barrel flange clip", then "gently advance the plunger driver toward the syringe plunger" until "it is flush with the syringe plunger". Japan's device regulator (PMDA Medical Safety Information No. 50, 2017) reports a patient case of a flange not in the slit: "the set drug volume will not be injected"; a driver not touching the plunger risks siphoning, and one pushed in gives an unplanned dose. Done by: nurses.
setup: Positions in cm on the table, from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left. A white syringe pump, fixed, centred at x 33, its cradle running along y: a body 5 cm wide (along x) whose cradle floor is 2.5 cm up, from y -5.5 to 4.45, with low side walls 1 mm clear of a seated barrel; the flange slot, 3.5 mm wide and 14 mm deep with a rounded mouth (5 mm radius), centred at y 5.125; past it, from y 5.8 to 14, the driver's track, and on it the grey plunger driver (4 cm wide, 2 cm long, 3 cm tall, with a black grip 12 by 6 mm on top) that slides along y and starts with its face at y 11.85, 3 cm from the plunger. The syringe, a stand-in for a 60 mL syringe: a clear barrel 29.6 mm across and 100 mm long with a nose at one end and at the other a flange 40 by 50 mm and 2.5 mm thick; 75 g. In it, a white plunger (a stopper, an 8 mm rod and a 30 mm square thumb disc, 12 g), pulled back full. The syringe lies on two black stands (2 by 1 cm, 2.6 cm tall) at x 25, its barrel's centre at y -20, flange toward the pump (left).
scoring: The syringe is in the cradle when its barrel's axis is within 3 mm of the cradle's centre line sideways, no more than 15 mm above its seat and within 15 degrees of the cradle's line. It is seated when the axis is within 1 mm of its seat (sideways and up), level within 1.5 degrees, and the flange's centre is within 0.8 mm of the slot's (it has 0.5 mm a side). The plunger is pushed in when its stopper has moved more than 1 mm toward the nose. Pushed in, or not in the cradle: 0. In the cradle, not seated (flange out of its slot, syringe cocked): 0.2. Seated: 0.5. Seated, the driver's face within 5 mm of the thumb disc: 0.75. Seated, the driver within 1 mm and everything still: 1.0, held for 1 s. Possible scores: 0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. To check a real trial: a side photo for the flange in its slot and the driver at the thumb disc, and the syringe's graduations for the plunger unmoved.
reset_notes: Pull the driver back to its start, take the syringe out and lay it on its stands flange toward the pump, with the plunger pulled back full.
fidelity: Stand-in sizes for a 60 mL syringe. The barrel is 16 flat staves. The stopper slides with little friction (a real one needs a firm push to start), so the scorer allows 1 mm of plunger travel from the driver's contact. The flange slot's mouth is rounded like a clip's lead-in. The driver slides without its release lever, and there is no barrel clamp.
